title: IntersectionObserver for reveal, lazy load and scroll spy
when: Something must happen when an element enters the viewport: reveal on scroll, load more items, highlight the current section, pause media.
prompt:
Goal: Viewport reactions without scroll listeners: cheap, accessible and correct when observed elements change.
Steps:
1. One observer per purpose: { rootMargin: "200px 0px", threshold: 0 } for preloading, threshold 0.5 for mostly visible.
2. In the callback check entry.isIntersecting and unobserve elements whose job is done.
3. Infinite list: observe a sentinel after the last item; when visible and not loading, fetch the next page; at the end stop and show "No more items".
4. Scroll spy: observe sections with rootMargin "-40% 0px -55% 0px" and set aria-current="true" on the matching nav link.
5. Reveal: add a class that transitions opacity; under prefers-reduced-motion skip movement; content stays visible if the script fails.
6. disconnect() when the view is removed.
Quality bar:
- No scroll event listeners for these effects.
- Content is readable with scripts off.
- Infinite lists also offer a Load more button.
Pitfalls:
- Hiding content in CSS until the observer runs.
- Thousands of separate observers.
- Triggering a load again while one is pending.
Verify:
- [ ] unobserve or disconnect used.
- [ ] Reduced motion rule for reveal styles.
- [ ] Loading flag guards the sentinel.
- [ ] aria-current on the active link.
Output: js/observe.js with the helpers, plus the CSS classes they toggle.

examples.input: carregar mais produtos quando chegar no fim da página
examples.output: sentinel observed with 200px rootMargin, loading flag, Load more button fallback, end message
